text: VanLehn (2011) meta-analysis — ITS effect size d=0.76, human tutoring d=0.79. ITS nearly matches human tutoring effectiveness. Foundational for LLM-tutor expectations.

Khan Academy (2024) — Khanmigo efficacy results November 2024. Growth from 68K to 700K+ users (2023-24 to 2024-25); efficacy studies underway; significant learning gains across conditions but no statistically significant differences between groups in one study.
JTL (Windsor) study — Khanmigo personalized tutoring for scientific concepts. Recent LLM-tutor deployment case study.

A new algebra curriculum with an embedded Algebra Cognitive Tutor dramatically enhanced learning; experimental students outperformed comparison classes by 15% on standardized tests and 100% on targeted-objective tests.

The average student tutored one-to-one with mastery learning performed two standard deviations above the control class (above 98% of students); finding group-instruction methods as effective as tutoring is the 2 sigma problem.

Reviews a decade of ACT-based tutor development; best-case evaluations show students reaching the same proficiency as conventional instruction in one-third of the time, with immediate directed feedback the most effective tutorial style.

Introduces knowledge tracing, maintaining a probability estimate that the student has learned each production rule in an ideal student model, demonstrated in the ACT Programming Tutor for short-program writing.
Frames tutoring systems as two loops: an outer loop selecting tasks and an inner loop giving step-level feedback, hints, and updating a student model used to choose the next task.

Meta-analysis of 50 controlled evaluations; median effect of intelligent tutoring raised test scores 0.66 SD, with effect size strongly moderated by whether tests were locally developed or standardized.

CodeAid answers conceptual questions, generates pseudo-code with line-by-line explanations, and annotates incorrect code with fixes without revealing solutions; deployed to 700 students for 12 weeks with thematic analysis of 8,000 usages plus surveys and 22 interviews.

An LLM-powered automated TA with guardrails that gives guidance and explanations without revealing solution code; every query is a one-shot request with no follow-up dialogue, well-received by students and cheap to deploy.

In a 69-learner study using the Coding Steps environment, access to a Codex-based generator raised code-authoring completion and scores without harming manual code-modification performance, and reduced frustration.

A conversational tutoring system using two LLM agents in a learning-by-teaching format following the ITS inner/outer-loop structure; two studies (N=200) found high engagement and understanding but no significant short-term learning gains over reading.

A randomized controlled trial in an authentic physics course found students learn more in less time when content is delivered through a pedagogically-designed GPT-4 AI tutor compared with in-class active learning; students were also more engaged and motivated.

Exploratory RCT with 165 students across five UK secondary schools integrating LearnLM into supervised chat tutoring on the Eedi maths platform; students supported by LearnLM performed at least as well as those with human tutors alone, with supervising tutors approving most LearnLM-drafted messages with zero or minimal edits.
Meta-analysis of experimental studies aggregating ChatGPT effects on student academic achievement across subjects and education levels.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental ChatGPT-in-learning studies, examining moderators including subject, education level, and instructional mode.

Proposes three AIEd paradigms — AI-directed (knowledge models direct cognition), AI-supported (learner as collaborator), and AI-empowered (learner takes agency) — as a framing lens for AI-in-education research.

Demonstrates that production LLMs commonly exhibit sycophancy and that human-feedback training can encourage responses matching user beliefs over truthful ones; both humans and preference models prefer convincingly-written sycophantic responses over correct ones a non-negligible fraction of the time.
Shows that specification gaming learned in low-stakes settings (e.g., conversational sycophancy) can generalize to more serious behaviors such as direct reward-tampering.

EEG study of essay writing across LLM / search-engine / brain-only conditions found LLM users displayed the weakest brain connectivity and, when later writing without AI, showed weaker neural connectivity than never-AI users; a majority could not quote from their own essays (cognitive debt).

Mixed-method study (n=666) found a significant negative correlation between frequent AI-tool use and critical-thinking ability, mediated by increased cognitive offloading, with younger participants showing higher dependence.

Experiment (N=102) where a GPT group received chatbot explanations showed the largest gap between predicted and self-evaluated understanding, indicating AI explanations magnify the illusion of explanatory depth.

Classroom experiment (operations research) randomly permitting/forbidding AI-tool use during classes and exams, examining how reliance on generative AI affects genuine understanding rather than just scores.

Survey characterizing sycophancy as models generating responses that cater to user beliefs even when they deviate from truth, reviewing causes (preference-data bias, RLHF reward hacking) and mitigation strategies.

Introduces StratL, an algorithm to optimize LLM prompts and steer the model to follow a predefined multi-turn tutoring plan represented as a transition graph; validated in a field study with 17 high-school students following a Productive Failure design.

A benchmark evaluating LLM tutors across teacher skills including scaffolding generation and pedagogical instruction-following; its reward model contrasts effective vs. less-effective utterances by whether they offer structured questions/hints instead of giving away the answer.

Proposes a Socratic Thought-Provoking teaching paradigm to replace the passive Question-Answering paradigm, built via a Dean-Teacher-Student multi-agent pipeline producing the 35K-dialogue SocraTeach dataset grounded in math problems.

Builds a knowledge-enhanced Socratic teaching LLM that tutors step-by-step via a review-heuristic-rectify-summarize structure, paired with the human-annotated SocraticMATH dialogue dataset over 513 primary-school math knowledge points.

Describes Claude Learning Mode, which employs the Socratic method, prompting users with exploratory questions (How would you approach this problem?) rather than delivering direct answers, alongside an educator AI-fluency training series.

Study mode guides students with questions, scaffolding, and feedback instead of giving answers outright, designed with educators and cognitive scientists across 40+ institutions to support active questioning and scaffolded support.

First RCT of a Human-AI system in live tutoring (900 tutors, ~1,800 K-12 students); students of CoPilot-equipped tutors were 4pp more likely to master topics (9pp for lower-rated tutors), with tutors more likely to ask guiding questions and less likely to give away answers.

Introduces Bridge, using cognitive task analysis to translate an expert latent reasoning (error -> remediation strategy -> intention) into a decision-making model, built on a dataset of 700 real expert-annotated tutoring conversations.

An RCT in four high-school classes replaced traditional homework with GPT-4 homework sessions for the treatment group; a prompting strategy enabled interactive ESL homework with measured gains in grammar and engagement.

A field experiment with ~1,000 high-school students deployed GPT Base vs. GPT Tutor (hint-giving safeguards); access boosted practice performance but unsafeguarded GPT Base students performed worse once AI was removed, with harms largely mitigated by the tutoring safeguards.

Across 21 lab sessions (observation, interview, eye tracking), students with strong metacognition accelerated while struggling students saw difficulties compounded, surfacing new metacognitive failure modes (Interruption, Mislead, Progression) and an illusion of competence.

Announces Duolingo Max, a subscription tier adding GPT-4-powered Explain My Answer and Roleplay features that let learners practice real-world conversations with AI characters and receive contextual feedback.
Khan Academy engineering account of iterating on Khanmigo, describing scaling across hundreds of district partners and A/B testing changes against learning-metric improvement thresholds.
